questions.q: What does AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS do, and what is its default?
options: Lets the optimizer create missing single-column statistics on the fly when needed; default ON
Automatically creates indexes on every column; default OFF
Deletes old statistics automatically; default ON
Only applies to tempdb; default OFF
questions.explain: AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS is ON by default and lets the optimizer generate single-column statistics automatically for columns that lack them but are used in predicates.

questions.q: Why does stale statistics matter to the query optimizer?
options: It's one of the most common causes of the optimizer picking a bad execution plan
Stale statistics have no effect on plan choice
Stale statistics only affect backup performance
Stale statistics only matter in SIMPLE recovery model
questions.explain: The optimizer relies on statistics to estimate row counts and choose a plan; stale statistics lead to bad row-count estimates and, frequently, bad plans.

questions.q: What is AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC's default, and what does turning it ON change?
options: Default OFF; turning it ON makes the stats refresh happen in the background instead of blocking the triggering query
Default ON; turning it ON disables statistics entirely
Default ON; turning it ON forces synchronous updates on every query
Default OFF; turning it ON deletes existing statistics
questions.explain: AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC is OFF by default. Turning it ON means the query that triggers a stats refresh runs immediately with the slightly-stale statistics while the update happens asynchronously, avoiding a latency spike.

questions.q: In which scenario is turning AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC ON most justified?
options: A large, high-concurrency OLTP table where synchronous stat updates cause visible, unpredictable query latency spikes
A small, rarely-touched lookup table
A database in SIMPLE recovery model, unconditionally
It should never be turned on under any circumstances
questions.explain: The async option trades slightly-stale statistics for smoother latency — most valuable on large, busy OLTP tables where an unpredictable synchronous pause is the bigger problem.

questions.q: For the majority of databases, what is the recommended posture on AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS and AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS?
options: Leave both ON — they're the right default almost everywhere
Turn both OFF to save CPU
Turn AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS OFF but leave AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS OFF too
They must always be turned OFF in FULL recovery model
questions.explain: AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS and AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS should stay ON in nearly every real environment; turning them off is reserved for tightly-controlled setups with manual statistics management.
